Among 3195 residents, 526 suspected ARI episodes occurred. [10.1016/j.jamda.2026.106435]

news.headline_zh: Clover 2 期试验显示 RSV-hMPV 疫苗抗体显著上升。
news.lead_zh: Clover 在澳大利亚对 420 名 60 至 85 岁成年人进行的 2 期试验显示,其 RSV-hMPV 疫苗候选药物 SCB-1022 和 SCB-1033 引发了显著的中和抗体反应。
key_findings_zh: 疫苗组中和抗体对 RSV 和 hMPV 的反应分别提升了 6-9 倍和 6-8 倍。
添加 PIV3 抗原未引发免疫干扰,可能增强疫苗保护范围。
未发现严重不良事件,多数不良反应轻微且在两天内缓解。
疫苗组呼吸道感染率较安慰剂组降低 62%,但基于不良事件报告。
Clover 已完成三种抗原的商业化生产,降低制造风险。
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 疫苗在老年人群中显示出良好的免疫反应和安全性,但需进一步验证其实际疗效。
news.caveats_zh: 结果基于不良事件报告,未通过 PCR 确认感染情况。
news.headline_en: Clover's Phase 2 Trial Shows Significant Antibody Rise for RSV-hMPV Vaccine.
news.lead_en: Clover's Phase 2 trial of its RSV-hMPV vaccine candidates, SCB-1022 and SCB-1033, showed significant neutralizing antibody rises in 420 adults aged 60 to 85 in Australia.
key_findings_en: Neutralizing antibody responses increased 6-9 times for RSV and 6-8 times for hMPV at 28 days post-vaccination.
No immune interference was observed when PIV3 antigen was added, suggesting broader protection for those with pre-existing immunity.
No serious adverse events were reported, with most solicited adverse events being mild and resolving within two days.
Vaccinated participants had a 62% lower rate of respiratory tract infections, though based on adverse event reporting rather than PCR confirmation.
Clover has completed commercial-scale production of all three antigen components, reducing manufacturing risks.
news.trend_or_risk_en: The vaccine demonstrated strong immune responses and safety in older adults, but further validation in Phase 3 trials is needed to confirm its efficacy.
news.caveats_en: The findings are hypothesis-generating and require outcomes-based validation in Phase 3 trials.
news.brief_en: Clover has announced positive Phase 2 clinical data for its RSV + hMPV ± PIV3 respiratory combination vaccine candidates in older adults. The trial, conducted in Australia with 420 participants, was a randomized, observer-blinded, multi-center study. Results showed a 62% lower rate of respiratory tract infections in the vaccine groups compared to the placebo group within 28 days of vaccination, based on adverse event reporting. Neutralizing antibody responses were observed, with fold rises of 6-9 for RSV, 6-8 for hMPV, and greater than 3 for PIV3. The findings are preliminary, as no PCR sequencing was performed to confirm infection cases. The study validates Clover's Trimer-Tag platform for developing multi-valent protein-based respiratory vaccines, which could impact public health and chronic diseases caused by respiratory viruses. The results are part of ongoing research and do not yet indicate the vaccine's full efficacy or safety profile.

news.en: Clover's Phase 2 trial of its RSV-hMPV vaccine candidates, SCB-1022 and SCB-1033, showed significant neutralizing antibody rises in 420 adults aged 60 to 85 in Australia. Neutralizing antibody responses increased 6-9 times for RSV and 6-8 times for hMPV at 28 days post-vaccination. No immune interference was observed when PIV3 antigen was added, suggesting broader protection for those with pre-existing immunity. No serious adverse events were reported, with most solicited adverse events being mild and resolving within two days. Vaccinated participants had a 62% lower rate of respiratory tract infections, though based on adverse event reporting rather than PCR confirmation.

papers.title: Epidemiological Characteristics and Evolutionary Characterization of Human Metapneumovirus in Jiaxing, China
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) represents a leading cause of both upper and lower respiratory tract infections among children and adults globally. To investigate the prevalence and evolution of hMPV in the Jiaxing area of China between 2023 and 2025, we screened 3600 pharyngeal swab specimens by real-time PCR, identified 101 positives, and obtained genomic sequences of 48 viral isolates using high-throughput sequencing. Using the sequencing data, we reconstructed a phylogenetic tree and examined amino acid substitutions. The epidemiological analysis revealed an overall hMPV positivity rate of 2.81% (101/3600) in Jiaxing during 2023–2025. Although positive cases were detected across all age groups, they were mainly children, with no significant difference between genders. Regarding seasonal patterns, the peak of hMPV activity occurred predominantly during winter and spring. Over the study period, four genotypes co-circulated, in the order of B2 (41.67%), A2.2.2 (37.50%), A2.2.1 (16.67%), and B1 (4.17%). Further phylogenetic analysis showed that the B1 strains from Jiaxing clustered primarily with those from Beijing, China, while B2, A2.2.1, and A2.2.2 strains were more closely related to strains from the United States and Beijing. Of note, an A2c111nt-dup variant was identified in Jiaxing in 2023. Starting from November 2024, the prevailing genotype transitioned from A2.2.1/A2.2.2 to B2, and B2 emerged as the absolutely dominant strain by 2025. In comparison with earlier circulating strains, several amino acid substitutions have accumulated in current isolates, such as T223N, D280N, I392T, R396Q, S444N, K450R, and T521A in the F protein of B2 strains. Furthermore, the G, L, P, and SH proteins also displayed temporally patterned amino acid replacements. While the biological significance of these mutations is yet to be determined, these results highlight the public health importance of ongoing hMPV surveillance and dynamic monitoring of its genetic evolution.

source_records.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) represents a leading cause of both upper and lower respiratory tract infections among children and adults globally. To investigate the prevalence and evolution of hMPV in the Jiaxing area of China between 2023 and 2025, we screened 3600 pharyngeal swab specimens by real-time PCR, identified 101 positives, and obtained genomic sequences of 48 viral isolates using high-throughput sequencing. Using the sequencing data, we reconstructed a phylogenetic tree and examined amino acid substitutions. The epidemiological analysis revealed an overall hMPV positivity rate of 2.81% (101/3600) in Jiaxing during 2023–2025. Although positive cases were detected across all age groups, they were mainly children, with no significant difference between genders. Over the study period, four genotypes co-circulated, in the order of B2 (41.67%), A2.2.2 (37.50%), A2.2.1 (16.67%), and B1 (4.17%). Further phylogenetic analysis showed that the B1 strains from Jiaxing clustered primarily with those from Beijing, China, while B2, A2.2.1, and A2.2.2 strains were more closely related to strains from the United States and Beijing. papers.title: Clinical Impact of Acute Respiratory Virus Infections in Nursing Home Residents
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the suspected acute respiratory infection (ARI) risk and the clinical impact of a range of respiratory viruses in Dutch nursing home (NH) residents. DESIGN: Prospective cohort study (March 2023-May 2025). SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Residents from 15 Dutch NHs were enrolled when suspected of an ARI. METHODS: Clinical data were collected on days 0, 14, and 28. Residual nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs were tested for a broad respiratory virus panel. A Bayesian multilevel logistic model including seasonal and NH-level random effects estimated suspected ARI risk. Relative clinical outcomes were compared by virus. RESULTS: Among 3195 residents, 526 suspected ARI episodes occurred. The estimated suspected ARI risk was 10.2% (95% credible interval, 1.7-43.8). Viruses were identified in 291 episodes: severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2; 29.0%), influenza A virus (23.6%), rhinovirus/enterovirus (18.8%), respiratory syncytial virus (11.8%), human metapneumovirus (hMPV; 6.4%), parainfluenza viruses (5.1%), and human coronaviruses (5.4%). hMPV and respiratory syncytial virus tended to be associated with higher odds of moderate or severe disease, and hMPV was linked to a 4-fold increase in bed hours. Influenza A was associated with delayed recovery, oxygen requirement, and a 3-fold risk of secondary bacterial pneumonia. SARS-CoV-2 cases had higher estimated odds of recovery by day 14 and spent fewer additional hours in bed during ARI episodes. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Influenza remains a major contributor to ARI burden in NH residents, whereas SARS-CoV-2 has relatively limited impact. The pronounced clinical impact of hMPV suggests its relevance for ARI management in this population.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the clinical impact of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) in Dutch nursing home residents, focusing on human metapneumovirus (hMPV). A prospective cohort study was conducted from March 2023 to May 2025, enrolling residents suspected of an ARI. Clinical data were collected on days 0, 14, and 28, and residual swabs were tested for a broad range of respiratory viruses. Among 3195 residents, 526 ARI episodes were recorded, with hMPV identified in 6.4% of cases. The study found that hMPV was associated with higher odds of moderate or severe disease and a 4-fold increase in bed hours. These findings suggest that hMPV has a significant clinical impact in this population, emphasizing the need for improved surveillance and management strategies. The study's observational design limits causal conclusions, but the use of a Bayesian multilevel logistic model and comprehensive virus testing strengthens the evidence.

papers.title_zh: 疗养院居民急性呼吸道病毒感染的临床影响
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the suspected acute respiratory infection (ARI) risk and the clinical impact of a range of respiratory viruses in Dutch nursing home (NH) residents. DESIGN: Prospective cohort study (March 2023-May 2025). SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Residents from 15 Dutch NHs were enrolled when suspected of an ARI. METHODS: Clinical data were collected on days 0, 14, and 28. Residual nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs were tested for a broad respiratory virus panel. A Bayesian multilevel logistic model including seasonal and NH-level random effects estimated suspected ARI risk. Relative clinical outcomes were compared by virus. RESULTS: Among 3195 residents, 526 suspected ARI episodes occurred. The estimated suspected ARI risk was 10.2% (95% credible interval, 1.7-43.8). Viruses were identified in 291 episodes: severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2; 29.0%), influenza A virus (23.6%), rhinovirus/enterovirus (18.8%), respiratory syncytial virus (11.8%), human metapneumovirus (hMPV; 6.4%), parainfluenza viruses (5.1%), and human coronaviruses (5.4%). hMPV and respiratory syncytial virus tended to be associated with higher odds of moderate or severe disease, and hMPV was linked to a 4-fold increase in bed hours. Influenza A was associated with delayed recovery, oxygen requirement, and a 3-fold risk of secondary bacterial pneumonia. SARS-CoV-2 cases had higher estimated odds of recovery by day 14 and spent fewer additional hours in bed during ARI episodes. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Influenza remains a major contributor to ARI burden in NH residents, whereas SARS-CoV-2 has relatively limited impact. The pronounced clinical impact of hMPV suggests its relevance for ARI management in this population.

papers.title: Human metapneumovirus prevention in children: emerging roles of monoclonal antibodies and vaccines
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a major cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection in children, older adults, and individuals with underlying medical conditions. In pediatric populations, hMPV contributes substantially to hospitalizations, morbidity, and healthcare costs, yet no licensed vaccine or monoclonal antibody is currently available for prevention. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on emerging preventive strategies against hMPV, with particular emphasis on monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and vaccines for children. Advances in structural virology have identified the fusion glycoprotein as the principal target of neutralizing immunity and have provided a rationale for the development of hMPV-specific and cross-reactive RSV–hMPV mAbs. Several mAbs have shown potent neutralizing activity and protection in animal models, although clinical development remains limited. Vaccine development has progressed across multiple platforms, including live-attenuated, mRNA, protein-subunit, virus-like particle, and viral-vectored vaccines. However, key challenges remain, particularly regarding immunogenicity in seronegative infants, risk of enhanced respiratory disease, durability of protection, seasonality, and optimal target populations. Current evidence suggests that hMPV prevention in children will likely require a layered strategy combining maternal immunization, active vaccination during late infancy, and targeted protection for high-risk children beyond infancy.

papers.title_zh: 儿童 人偏肺病毒 预防:单克隆抗体和 疫苗 的新作用
papers.source_body_en: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a major cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection in children, older adults, and individuals with underlying medical conditions. In pediatric populations, hMPV contributes substantially to hospitalizations, morbidity, and healthcare costs, yet no licensed vaccine or monoclonal antibody is currently available for prevention. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on emerging preventive strategies against hMPV, with particular emphasis on monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and vaccines for children. Advances in structural virology have identified the fusion glycoprotein as the principal target of neutralizing immunity and have provided a rationale for the development of hMPV-specific and cross-reactive RSV–hMPV mAbs. Several mAbs have shown potent neutralizing activity and protection in animal models, although clinical development remains limited. Vaccine development has progressed across multiple platforms, including live-attenuated, mRNA, protein-subunit, virus-like particle, and viral-vectored vaccines. However, key challenges remain, particularly regarding immunogenicity in seronegative infants, risk of enhanced respiratory disease, durability of protection, seasonality, and optimal target populations. Current evidence suggests that hMPV prevention in children will likely require a layered strategy combining maternal immunization, active vaccination during late infancy, and targeted protection for high-risk children beyond infancy.
papers.abstract_zh: 人偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 是儿童、老年人和患有基础疾病的人急性 下呼吸道感染 的主要原因。在儿科人群中,hMPV 极大地增加了住院率、发病率和医疗费用,但目前尚无获得许可的 疫苗 或单克隆抗体可用于预防。这篇叙述性综述总结了针对 hMPV 的新兴预防策略的当前证据,特别强调了针对儿童的单克隆抗体 (mAb) 和 疫苗。结构病毒学的进展已确定融合糖蛋白是中和免疫的主要靶标,并为开发 hMPV 特异性和交叉反应性 RSV-hMPV 单克隆抗体提供了理论基础。尽管临床开发仍然有限,但几种单克隆抗体在动物模型中显示出有效的中和活性和保护作用。疫苗 的开发已在多个平台上取得进展,包括减毒活、mRNA、蛋白质亚基、病毒样颗粒和病毒载体 疫苗。然而,关键挑战仍然存在,特别是在血清阴性婴儿的免疫原性、呼吸道疾病增强的风险、保护的持久性、季节性和最佳目标人群方面。目前的证据表明,儿童 hMPV 预防可能需要采取分层策略,结合母亲免疫、婴儿后期积极的 疫苗接种 以及对婴儿期后高危儿童的有针对性的保护。

papers.title: Emerging Trends in the Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management of Human Metapneumovirus-Associated Respiratory Infections
papers.abstract: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

papers.title_zh: 发病机制、诊断 和 人偏肺病毒 相关呼吸道感染管理的新趋势
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.
papers.abstract_zh: 引言:人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是一种重要的呼吸道病原体,可在不同年龄段人群中引发感染,尤其是在幼儿、免疫功能低下者及老年人中。尽管其具有重要的临床意义,但目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物或针对人偏肺病毒的特异性治疗方法,亟需进一步研究治疗和预防策略。方法:通过系统性文献综述,检索同行评议期刊、临床试验及近期研究,重点关注人偏肺病毒感染。提取并分析数据,以评估抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体、免疫调节剂及疫苗候选物的有效性。结果:研究表明,人偏肺病毒主要靶向呼吸道上皮细胞,触发免疫应答,这些免疫应答既有助于病毒清除,也会导致疾病发病机制。正在研发的治疗方法,包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂,显示出潜力,但仍需进一步验证。免疫调节剂和中草药可能提供支持性益处,但其对人偏肺病毒的有效性尚未得到证实。疫苗研发取得进展,多个候选疫苗已进入临床前及早期临床阶段。讨论:由于人偏肺病毒的季节性流行、与其他呼吸道病毒的临床相似性以及缺乏特异性治疗方法,该病毒继续对公共卫生构成重大负担。该病毒通过多种机制逃避免疫应答,导致疾病严重程度增加,尤其是在易感人群中。尽管目前主要采用支持性治疗,但新兴的抗病毒药物和疫苗可能为未来提供解决方案。改善诊断可及性、提高公众意识及开展针对性研究对于控制人偏肺病毒感染至关重要。结论:由于缺乏针对性治疗方法和疫苗,人偏肺病毒继续对公共卫生构成挑战。针对抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体及疫苗的持续研究对于有效疾病管理至关重要。亟需进一步临床试验以确立安全有效的治疗方案。

papers.title: Transcriptional signatures of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection using relaxed magnitude altitude score with hub-centric network analysis (RMAS-HCNA)
papers.abstract: Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus A (RSVA) and respiratory syncytial virus B (RSVB) may induce distinct airway host responses. We compared them with influenza A virus (IAV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in airway organ tissue equivalents (OTEs) and developed the Relaxed Magnitude Altitude Score with Hub-Centric Network Analysis framework (RMAS-HCNA). Methods OTEs were infected with RSVA-GFP5 or RSVB-GFP3 at low multiplicity of infection and profiled at 24 and 72 h using the NanoString nCounter Host Response Panel. Previous IAV and hMPV profiles were integrated. Analyses included source-matched differential expression, cross-virus ranking, network-based module selection, nested cross-validation, and Gene Ontology Biological Process enrichment. Results RSVA showed the strongest temporal expansion and developed a late response centered on intracellular transport, localization, and organelle organization. RSVB remained the most restricted response, shifting from early inflammatory and signaling-associated activity to a later interferon-stimulated profile. IAV maintained a broad antiviral response, whereas hMPV combined limited induction with extensive late downregulation of stress, catabolic, metabolic, and transport-related processes. A shared antiviral component was present across infections, while downregulated responses were largely virus dependent. Under five-fold outer and four-fold inner nested cross-validation, the selected genes achieved a mean outer-test Macro F1 of 0.859 and balanced accuracy of 0.888, compared with 0.604 and 0.616 for the all-gene comparator. Discussion The four viruses shared an antiviral foundation but followed distinct temporal and functional trajectories. The framework identified compact, biologically representative panels that generalized better than the complete measured gene set, although independent genome-wide and in vivo validation remains necessary.

papers.title: Etiology and Clinical Manifestations of Acute Respiratory Infections in Pediatric Patients: A Retrospective Study in Moscow, Russia
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Acute respiratory viral infections (ARVIs) are the leading cause of pediatric morbidity and exhibit considerable clinical heterogeneity. The analysis of clinical and etiological associations, as well as the identification of factors linked to severe ARVI cases, is essential for effective epidemiological surveillance. Methods: A retrospective, single-center observational study was conducted including 1362 non-COVID-19 pediatric cases of acute respiratory infections (ARIs), registered between 2021 and 2024. Viral pathogens were detected using real-time PCR for broad-spectrum screening of respiratory viruses. Results: Viral etiology was established in approximately 50% of cases. The most frequently detected pathogen was Human rhinovirus (HRV) (35.6%), followed by Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and Human adenovirus (HAdV). Despite its predominance, HRV did not demonstrate nosological specificity. The strongest associations with lower respiratory tract infections were identified for RSV (OR = 3.2) and Human bocavirus (HBoV; OR = 2.4), predominantly within the pneumonia category. RSV was also associated with bronchitis/bronchiolitis (OR = 1.8). Significant associations with upper respiratory tract infections were established for Influenza viruses (OR = 10.4) and HAdV, including nasopharyngitis (OR = 3.88) and acute tonsillitis (OR = 3.9). HAdV additionally demonstrated an association with otitis media (OR = 5.1). Severe disease was registered in 52.3% of all clinical observations and occurred most frequently among young children, particularly in cases associated with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV >80%), as well as with human bocavirus (HBoV) and Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) (~55–59%). Co-infections were not associated with increased disease severity compared with monoinfections (OR = 1.1). Conclusions: The obtained results highlight the contribution of specific etiological agents to severe respiratory infections in children. These findings support the prioritization of such pathogens in clinical diagnostics, including the design of diagnostic algorithms and the selection of patient management strategies in pediatric populations.

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 获得的结果强调了特定病原体对儿童严重呼吸道感染的影响。这些发现支持临床诊断中此类病原体的优先顺序,包括诊断算法的设计和儿科人群患者管理策略的选择。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为儿童严重呼吸道感染,特别是由呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和人偏肺病毒(HMPV)引起的儿童严重呼吸道感染制定有针对性的诊断策略和管理方案提供参考。

papers.title: Metapneumovirus genomes harbor a non-random layer of reverse ORFs
papers.abstract: Abstract Metapneumoviruses (MPVs) are negative-sense RNA viruses associated with recurrent respiratory disease outbreaks, yet their full coding potential remains incompletely characterized. We performed a genome-scale survey of reverse open reading frames (rORFs) located on the negative-sense genomic RNA across human metapneumovirus (HMPV) and related MPV genomes, benchmarking against codon-aware and composition-preserving null models. At the recurrent P-overlapping locus, we identified an unusually long rORF (244 aa) overlapping most of the phosphoprotein (P) gene; the HMPV reference genome contains a shorter variant at the same locus (186 aa), which we term P-AS1. Across the dataset, the upper tail of rORF lengths and their clustering into recurrent hotspots exceeded expectations under both controls, consistent with non-random organization. In sequence- and structure-based analyses of selected HMPV reference rORF candidates, several showed features consistent with small membrane-associated proteins, including predicted transmembrane helices. AlphaFold-based modeling of rORF90 suggested a pore-like oligomeric assembly consistent with a tentative viroporin-like hypothesis, although the model remains hypothesis-generating and does not demonstrate expression or function. We assessed translational permissiveness using initiation-site prediction and a Kozak-like start-context screen, supporting prioritization of selected candidates without implying in vivo translation. Together, these analyses support a non-random layer of rORFs in MPV genomes and provide candidates and resources for targeted experimental validation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the coding potential of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) genomes, particularly focusing on the presence of reverse open reading frames (rORFs) and their potential biological significance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a genome-scale survey of rORFs in HMPV and related MPV genomes, comparing findings against codon-aware and composition-preserving null models to assess non-random organization.
analysis.methods: The researchers performed a genome-scale survey of reverse open reading frames (rORFs) in human metapneumovirus (HMPV) and related MPV genomes, using codon-aware and composition-preserving null models for benchmarking.
analysis.main_results: At the recurrent P-overlapping locus, an unusually long rORF (244 aa) overlapping most of the phosphoprotein (P) gene was identified, while the HMPV reference genome contained a shorter variant (186 aa) termed P-AS1. Additionally, sequence- and structure-based analyses of selected HMPV reference rORF candidates revealed features consistent with small membrane-associated proteins, including predicted transmembrane helices.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that MPV genomes harbor a non-random layer of rORFs, which may have functional implications, although the study does not confirm expression or function of these rORFs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide candidates and resources for targeted experimental validation of rORFs in human metapneumovirus, which could inform future research on viral coding potential and its role in disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on computational modeling and does not demonstrate in vivo expression or function of the identified rORFs, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the presence of reverse open reading frames (rORFs) in human metapneumovirus (HMPV) and related MPV genomes. The researchers conducted a genome-scale survey, benchmarking against null models to assess non-random organization. They identified an unusually long rORF overlapping the phosphoprotein (P) gene and a shorter variant in the HMPV reference genome. Sequence- and structure-based analyses of selected rORF candidates revealed features consistent with small membrane-associated proteins. While these findings suggest a non-random layer of rORFs in MPV genomes, the study does not confirm their expression or function. The results provide candidates for targeted experimental validation, which could advance understanding of viral coding potential. However, the study's reliance on computational modeling limits its evidence strength, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

papers.title: Addressing the Sustainable Co-Management Strategy of Tourism Business and Government to Secure Tourist and Community Health-Safety against HMPV Respiratory
papers.abstract: Public health concerns involving respiratory infectious diseases can disrupt tourism operations, destination management, local economies, and community well-being. This study explored sustainable co-management strategies through which tourism businesses and government authorities can strengthen tourist and community health and safety in relation to human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-related respiratory health concerns. An exploratory qualitative design was employed, using semi-structured interviews with 20 purposively selected participants representing tourism businesses, government, public health, academia, and related stakeholder groups. Data were collected through face-to-face and online interviews in January and March 2026 and analysed thematically with support from NVivo. The analysis identified four interrelated themes: shared responsibility for tourist and host safety, compliance with health and safety guidelines, multi-stakeholder collaboration, and tourism resilience through sustainable co-management. Participants emphasised the importance of clear institutional roles, routine health and safety practices, timely communication, coordinated decision-making, preparedness, community participation, and collaboration between public and private stakeholders. The findings indicate that integrating health and safety considerations into routine tourism management may support preparedness and resilience while protecting visitors and host communities. However, the findings represent context-specific stakeholder perspectives rather than statistically generalisable evidence. The study provides a qualitative basis for further research on collaborative tourism governance, health-risk preparedness, and sustainable co-management in response to respiratory infectious-disease concerns.

papers.title: Clinical severity and co-infection of respiratory pathogens among children and adolescents with Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection in Guangzhou, China: a single-center retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) is a major cause of respiratory infections in children and adolescents. COVID-19 pandemic control measures may have disrupted the respiratory microenvironment and increased the risk of co-infection associated with severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Previous studies on MP co-infections were limited by small samples and lacked generalizability, with little evidence on MP-bacterial co-infection. This retrospective cohort study investigated co-infections and clinical severity in pediatric MP patients in Guangzhou. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, patients aged ≤ 18 years with confirmed MP infection were recruited from July 2023 to January 2024 in Guangzhou, China. Blood and/or respiratory specimens were collected for respiratory pathogen testing. Participants who completed testing for all 8 viral and 5 bacterial pathogens were included in the multivariable analyses. Multivariate logistic regression and negative binomial regression models were applied to investigate the co-infection patterns and clinical severity of MP infection. Findings A total of 1499 patients (mean [SD] age: 6.39 [3.49], 50.7% males) with confirmed MP infection were enrolled during the study period. The majority of patients (68%, 1020/1499) were hospitalized, among whom 62% (630/1020) had severe infection. HPIV (7.5%) was the most common co-pathogen with MP, followed by IFV (7.2%). MP-HPIV co-infection predominated from early July to late September 2023 and then decreased, while MP-IFV co-infection remained common throughout the study period. Hospitalized patients had a higher overall rate of MP-viral co-infection and MP-bacterial co-infection than outpatients. Multivariate analysis of the respiratory co-infection patterns revealed that co-infection of MP with adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, human parainfluenza virus, human rhinovirus, influenza A and B viruses, Klebsiella pneumoniae , or Streptococcus pneumoniae was associated with a significantly higher risk of severe clinical outcomes, longer hospital stay, and longer fever duration. Conclusions Children with MP infection were associated with the occurrence of severe disease, particularly those aged 0–5 years. These findings suggest that age-adapted clinical management strategies for MP cases should be developed, with special attention to specific co-infection patterns to improve the prognosis of MP infection.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted in Guangzhou, China, from July 2023 to January 2024. It included patients aged ≤ 18 years with confirmed MP infection who underwent testing for all 8 viral and 5 bacterial pathogens.
analysis.methods: Blood and/or respiratory specimens were collected for respiratory pathogen testing. Multivariate logistic regression and negative binomial regression models were used to analyze co-infection patterns and clinical severity.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that co-infection with human metapneumovirus was common among MP-infected patients, with HPIV (7.5%) being the most frequent co-pathogen, followed by IFV (7.2%).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the importance of considering co-infections in the clinical management of MP, particularly in identifying and addressing specific viral co-infection patterns to improve patient outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the clinical severity and co-infection patterns of Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) in children and adolescents in Guangzhou, China. It found that MP co-infections were common, with human metapneumovirus (HPIV) being the most frequent co-pathogen. The study highlights the need for age-adapted clinical strategies to address MP co-infections and improve patient outcomes. However, its single-center design may limit generalizability. The findings suggest that co-infection with HPIV or other pathogens is associated with more severe disease, emphasizing the importance of considering these patterns in clinical practice.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景肺炎支原体(MP)是儿童和青少年呼吸道感染的主要原因。COVID-19 大流行控制措施可能扰乱了呼吸道微环境,并增加了与严重社区获得性肺炎 (CAP) 相关的合并感染的风险。以往关于MP合并感染的研究样本有限,缺乏普遍性,MP与细菌合并感染的证据很少。这项回顾性 队列研究 研究调查了广州儿科 MP 患者的合并感染和临床严重程度。方法 在这项单中心回顾性 队列研究 研究中,招募了 2023 年 7 月至 2024 年 1 月在中国广州确诊的 18 岁以下确诊 MP 感染的患者。收集血液和/或呼吸道样本用于呼吸道病原体检测。完成所有 8 种病毒和 5 种细菌病原体检测的参与者均纳入多变量分析。应用多变量逻辑回归和负二项回归模型来研究 MP 感染的合并感染模式和临床严重程度。结果 研究期间共纳入了 1499 名确诊 MP 感染的患者(平均 [SD] 年龄:6.39 [3.49],50.7% 男性)。大多数患者(68%,1020/1499)住院治疗,其中62%(630/1020)有严重感染。HPIV (7.5%) 是 MP 最常见的共同病原体,其次是 IFV (7.2%)。从 2023 年 7 月初到 9 月下旬,MP-HPIV 合并感染占主导地位,然后有所下降,而 MP-IFV 合并感染在整个研究期间仍然很常见。住院患者MP-病毒合并感染率和MP-细菌合并感染率总体高于门诊患者。对呼吸道合并感染模式的多变量分析显示,MP与腺病毒、人偏肺病毒、人副流感病毒、人鼻病毒、甲型和乙型流感病毒、肺炎克雷伯菌或肺炎链球菌的合并感染与严重临床结果、住院时间更长和发热持续时间更长的风险显着升高相关。结论 儿童MP感染与重症的发生有关,尤其是0~5岁儿童。这些发现表明,应针对 MP 病例制定适合年龄的临床管理策略,特别关注特定的合并感染模式,以改善 MP 感染的预后。
papers.summary_zh: 摘要 背景肺炎支原体(MP)是儿童和青少年呼吸道感染的主要原因。COVID-19 大流行控制措施可能扰乱了呼吸道微环境,并增加了与严重社区获得性肺炎 (CAP) 相关的合并感染的风险。以往关于MP合并感染的研究样本有限,缺乏普遍性,MP与细菌合并感染的证据很少。这项回顾性 队列研究 研究调查了广州儿科 MP 患者的合并感染和临床严重程度。方法 在这项单中心回顾性 队列研究 研究中,招募了 2023 年 7 月至 2024 年 1 月在中国广州确诊的 18 岁以下确诊 MP 感染的患者。收集血液和/或呼吸道样本用于呼吸道病原体检测。完成所有 8 种病毒和 5 种细菌病原体检测的参与者均纳入多变量分析。应用多变量逻辑回归和负二项回归模型来研究 MP 感染的合并感染模式和临床严重程度。结果 研究期间共纳入了 1499 名确诊 MP 感染的患者(平均 [SD] 年龄:6.39 [3.49],50.7% 男性)。大多数患者(68%,1020/1499)住院治疗,其中62%(630/1020)有严重感染。HPIV (7.5%) 是 MP 最常见的共同病原体,其次是 IFV (7.2%)。从 2023 年 7 月初到 9 月下旬,MP-HPIV 合并感染占主导地位,然后有所下降,而 MP-IFV 合并感染在整个研究期间仍然很常见。住院患者MP-病毒合并感染率和MP-细菌合并感染率总体高于门诊患者。对呼吸道合并感染模式的多变量分析显示,MP与腺病毒、人偏肺病毒、人副流感病毒、人鼻病毒、甲型和乙型流感病毒、肺炎克雷伯菌或肺炎链球菌的合并感染与严重临床结果、住院时间更长和发热持续时间更长的风险显着升高相关。结论 儿童MP感染与重症的发生有关,尤其是0~5岁儿童。这些发现表明,应针对 MP 病例制定适合年龄的临床管理策略,特别关注特定的合并感染模式,以改善 MP 感染的预后。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 肺炎支原体(MP)是儿童和青少年呼吸道感染的主要原因。本研究旨在探讨 MP 与其他呼吸道病原体的临床严重程度和合并感染模式。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本单中心回顾性队列研究研究在中国广州进行,时间为2023年7月至2024年1月。研究纳入了年龄≤18岁、确诊MP感染并接受了所有8种病毒和5种细菌病原体检测的患者。
analysis_zh.methods: 收集血液和/或呼吸道样本用于呼吸道病原体检测。使用多变量逻辑回归和负二项回归模型来分析合并感染模式和临床严重程度。
analysis_zh.main_results: 共有 1499 名确诊 MP 感染的患者(平均 [SD] 年龄:6.39 [3.49],50.7% 男性)入组。大多数患者(68%,1020/1499)住院治疗,其中62%(630/1020)有严重感染。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,MP感染患者中与人偏肺病毒的共感染较为常见,其中HPIV(7.5%)是最常见的共感染病原体,其次是IFV(7.2%)。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了在 MP 临床管理中考虑合并感染的重要性,特别是在识别和解决特定病毒合并感染模式以改善患者预后方面。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 此前关于MP共感染的研究受限于样本量较小且缺乏可推广性。本研究提供了更全面的MP与病毒共感染数据,但其单中心设计可能影响结果的可推广性。

Adaptive Clinical Trial Design Adaptive Trial Design Addiction Psychiatry AI in Clinical Trials alcohol use disorder Alzheimer's Disease Article Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Trials Clinical Operations Clinical Research Clinical Trial Design Clinical Trial Operations Clinical Trial Ops Brief Clinical Trial Quality Clinical Trials CLINOPS WATCHDOG CNS Drug Development CNS Trials Conference Coverage Decentralized Clinical Trials Digital Health Technologies dual diagnosis eClinical Tech News eClinical Technology EMA Executive Interviews FDA Enforcement FDA Guidance FDA Real-World Evidence FDA Regulatory Strategy FDA Warning Letter GCP Compliance GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Oncology Trials Opinion Parkinson's Disease Platform Trials Psilocybin MDMA Psychedelic Clinical Trials PSYCH PULSE Real-World Evidence site activation Site Operations study startup Treatment-Resistant Depression Search for:Search Button Articles Conference Coverage Executive Interviews News CliniCast News Clover’s RSV-hMPV Vaccine Shows Antibody Rises in Phase 2 Trial By Jon Napitupulu September 7, 2026 More than half of American adults 75 and older have already received one of the approved RSV vaccines, which creates an awkward problem for any late-entrant vaccine: the target population has pre-existing immunity. Clover’s Phase 2 data, released September 6, is built around exactly that obstacle. In 420 adults aged 60 to 85 enrolled in Australia, SCB-1022 (RSV + hMPV) and SCB-1033 (RSV + hMPV + PIV3) produced 6-to-9-fold neutralizing antibody rises against RSV and 6-to-8-fold rises against hMPV at 28 days post-vaccination, with no drop-off in the oldest participants (75 and above) compared to those aged 60 to 74. The finding that matters most for competitive positioning is the absence of immune interference. Adding PIV3 antigen in SCB-1033 did not blunt RSV or hMPV responses compared to the two-pathogen formulation, and the company is explicitly positioning both candidates as options for people who already received Arexvy, Abrysvo, or mRESVIA to restore and broaden protection. That framing shifts the clinical question from “does it work?” to “does it add coverage that single-pathogen RSV vaccines cannot?” Phase 2 immunogenicity data cannot answer that definitively, but the pattern is consistent enough with Phase 1 to make the argument credible. Safety held up through the trial period. Solicited adverse events within seven days were mostly mild and resolved in about two days across both vaccine and placebo groups. There were no vaccine-related serious adverse events, no events of special interest, and no discontinuations. Separately, the company completed 2,000-liter commercial-scale bioreactor production of all three antigen components, which matters because manufacturing failures at scale have derailed protein-subunit programs before. Having that process validated before a pivotal trial removes one of the larger late-stage unknowns. The trial also captured an incidental signal: respiratory tract infection rates in vaccinated participants were roughly 62 percent lower than in placebo recipients within 28 days, though the study used adverse event reporting rather than PCR confirmation, so that number should be read as hypothesis-generating at best. Clover says it will evaluate mid- and late-stage development plans and seek global partnership opportunities, which means no Phase 3 start date is announced. CDC data from February 2026 puts RSV vaccination coverage at 43 percent among adults 75 and older, leaving a meaningful unvaccinated fraction, but the commercial case for a three-pathogen combination ultimately rests on demonstrating that broader coverage translates to fewer hospitalizations, not just higher antibody titers. That question requires an outcomes-powered Phase 3, and the readiness of a potential partner to fund it is the real variable to watch. Clover Announces Positive Phase 2 Clinical Data for RSV + hMPV ± PIV3 Respiratory Combination Vaccine Candidates in Older Adults PR Newswire Sun, September 6, 2026 at 6:07 PM CDT 6 min read 2197.HK +1.90% -- Positive Phase 2 (Australia) results strengthen potential best-in-class profile of RSV+hMPV±PIV3 combination vaccines, with the potential differentiated ability to re-vaccinate individuals previously receiving approved RSV vaccines to restore and broaden protection -- -- Robust neutralizing antibody responses across RSV, hMPV and PIV3 in Phase 2 recapitulates Phase 1 results demonstrating best-in-class breadth (with no immune interference) and no drop-off in responses in the oldest participants (75+ years) -- -- Favorable safety & tolerability profile and successful 2,000L commercial-scale production further de-risk late-stage development and commercialization -- SHANGHAI, Sept. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clover Biopharmaceuticals, Ltd. (Clover; HKEX: 02197), a global commercial-stage biotechnology company committed to unleashing the power of innovative vaccines to save lives and improve health around the world, today announced positive preliminary data from a Phase 2 clinical trial in older adults in Australia evaluating SCB-1022 (RSV + hMPV) and SCB-1033 (RSV + hMPV + PIV3) protein-based vaccine candidates based on prefusion-stabilized F (PreF)-Trimer subunit vaccine antigens utilizing Clover's validated Trimer-Tag vaccine technology platform. "We are pleased to announce positive Phase 2 clinical data strengthening the potential first-in-class and best-in-class profile for our RSV+hMPV±PIV3 combination vaccine candidates, with the potential differentiated ability to re-vaccinate individuals previously receiving approved RSV vaccines to restore and broaden protection," said Joshua Liang, Chief Executive Officer & Board Director of Clover. "The positive Phase 2 results significantly de-risk future late-stage development. Importantly, the results also continue to validate our differentiated Trimer-Tag platform for the development of multi-valent protein-based respiratory vaccines that have the potential to make an impact on public health and on chronic diseases caused by respiratory viruses[1]." The ongoing Phase 2 trial for Clover's combination vaccine candidates is a randomized, observer-blinded, multi-center study with 420 older adults (60-85 years) enrolled in Australia, and the participants have been randomized to receive either SCB-1022 (RSV + hMPV), SCB-1033 (RSV + hMPV + PIV3) or placebo. Immunogenicity Antibody titers (geometric mean titers [GMTs]) at 28 days post-vaccination in the Phase 2 were generally in-line with or trended higher than the prior Phase 1 trial. Geometric mean fold rises (GMFRs) in neutralizing antibodies (nAbs) at 28 days post-vaccination compared to pre-vaccination: RSV nAbs: Approximately 6-9 fold increases hMPV nAbs: Approximately 6-8 fold increases PIV3 nAbs: Greater than 3 fold increase (approximately 5 fold increase in participants with baseline PIV3 nAbs in the bottom tertile), driven by up to approximately 20 fold increases in PIV3 PreF-specific antibodies[2] No drop-off in antibody responses observed in the oldest participants (75+ years) compared to younger participants (60-74 years). No signs of immune interference on RSV and hMPV nAbs from the addition of PIV3 PreF antigen in SCB-1033 (RSV+hMPV+PIV3) compared to SCB-1022 (RSV+hMPV). Story Continues Respiratory Tract Infections (Based on AE Reporting) Approximately 62% lower rate of respiratory tract infection was observed in the vaccine groups (SCB-1022 and SCB-1033) versus the placebo group within 28 days of vaccination based on AE reporting of any respiratory tract infections (no PCR sequencing of infection cases was conducted in the study). Significant RSV outbreak[3] with co-circulation[4] of hMPV and PIV in Australia occurred during the study enrollment and follow-up period. Safety and Reactogenicity SCB-1022 and SCB-1033 were generally well-tolerated; solicited local and systemic adverse events (AEs) within 7 days of vaccination were mostly mild and all transient. The most common solicited AEs were fatigue, headache and injection site pain, with mean durations of approximately 2 days for the vaccine groups (SCB-1022 and SCB-1033) and the placebo group. The frequency of unsolicited AEs within 28 days of vaccination was similar across the vaccine and placebo groups. There were no vaccine-related serious adverse events (SAEs), AEs of special interest (AESIs), or AEs leading to discontinuation. Commercial-Scale Manufacturing Scale-Up In parallel with the Phase 2 trial, Clover conducted commercial-scale 2,000L bioreactor scale-up production of multiple batches of Trimer-Tagged RSV, hMPV and PIV3 PreF antigen components of SCB-1022/1033. The successful 2,000L production process scale-up further de-risk future late-stage development and commercialization. Based on these positive Phase 2 results for the RSV + hMPV ± PIV3 combination vaccine candidates further validating the Trimer-Tag platform, Clover will continue to evaluate continued mid- and late-stage development plans as well as potential global collaboration opportunities for value maximization. About Clover Clover Biopharmaceuticals is a global commercial-stage biotechnology company committed to unleashing the power of innovative vaccines to save lives and improve health around the world. With integrated research and development, manufacturing and commercial capabilities as well as strong partnerships with organizations globally, Clover has a diverse pipeline of candidates that have the potential to meaningfully reduce the burden of vaccine-preventable diseases—and to make more diseases preventable. [1] RSV and/or influenza vaccines have been demonstrated to reduce worsening of COPD, Asthma, cardiovascular disease (CVD) and chronic liver disease (CLD). Sources: (A) DOI: 10.1016/j.chest.2026.06.059 (CHEST Study), (B) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD002733.pub3, (C) DOI: 10.3389/fphar.2025.1701127, (D) DOI: 10.1136/bmjopen-2018-031070. [2] PIV3 PreF-specific nAbs (such as Site Ø and Site X) can potently neutralize the PIV3 virus (DOI: 10.1038/s41467-023-36459-3) , but unlike RSV and hMPV, the majority of pre-existing PIV3 nAbs at baseline are against the PIV3 HN protein (whereas levels of pre-existing PIV3 nAbs against the PIV3 PreF protein at baseline are low) (DOI: 10.1038/s41564-024-01722-w). Therefore, a numerically lower increase in total PIV3 nAbs induced by SCB-1033 (containing PIV3 PreF antigen) – as compared to increases in RSV and hMPV nAbs – is expected. [3] Australia Immunisation Coalition (Aus. Gov. Department of Health, National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System). Jan-May 2026. news.content_zh: Clover 宣布了其 RSV + hMPV ± PIV3 呼吸组合 疫苗 候选药物在老年人中的积极 2 期临床数据。该试验在澳大利亚进行,有 420 名年龄在 60-85 岁之间的参与者参加,是一项随机、观察者盲法、多中心研究。结果显示,根据不良事件报告,疫苗 组的呼吸道感染率在 疫苗 治疗 28 天内比安慰剂组降低了 62%。观察到中和抗体反应,RSV 增加 6-9 倍,hMPV 增加 6-8 倍,PIV3 增加超过 3 倍。这些结果是初步的,因为没有进行 PCR 测序来确认感染病例。该研究验证了 Clover 的 Trimer-Tag 平台可用于开发基于多价蛋白的呼吸道疾病 疫苗,该药物可能会影响公共卫生和呼吸道病毒引起的慢性疾病。该结果是正在进行的研究的一部分,尚未表明 疫苗 的全部功效或安全性。

Clover Announces Positive Phase 2 Clinical Data for RSV + hMPV ± PIV3 Respiratory Combination Vaccine Candidates in Older Adults PR Newswire Sun, September 6, 2026 at 6:07 PM CDT 6 min read 2197.HK -- Positive Phase 2 (Australia) results strengthen potential best-in-class profile of RSV+hMPV±PIV3 combination vaccines, with the potential differentiated ability to re-vaccinate individuals previously receiving approved RSV vaccines to restore and broaden protection -- -- Robust neutralizing antibody responses across RSV, hMPV and PIV3 in Phase 2 recapitulates Phase 1 results demonstrating best-in-class breadth (with no immune interference) and no drop-off in responses in the oldest participants (75+ years) -- -- Favorable safety & tolerability profile and successful 2,000L commercial-scale production further de-risk late-stage development and commercialization -- SHANGHAI, Sept. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clover Biopharmaceuticals, Ltd. (Clover; HKEX: 02197), a global commercial-stage biotechnology company committed to unleashing the power of innovative vaccines to save lives and improve health around the world, today announced positive preliminary data from a Phase 2 clinical trial in older adults in Australia evaluating SCB-1022 (RSV + hMPV) and SCB-1033 (RSV + hMPV + PIV3) protein-based vaccine candidates based on prefusion-stabilized F (PreF)-Trimer subunit vaccine antigens utilizing Clover's validated Trimer-Tag vaccine technology platform. "We are pleased to announce positive Phase 2 clinical data strengthening the potential first-in-class and best-in-class profile for our RSV+hMPV±PIV3 combination vaccine candidates, with the potential differentiated ability to re-vaccinate individuals previously receiving approved RSV vaccines to restore and broaden protection," said Joshua Liang, Chief Executive Officer & Board Director of Clover. "The positive Phase 2 results significantly de-risk future late-stage development. Importantly, the results also continue to validate our differentiated Trimer-Tag platform for the development of multi-valent protein-based respiratory vaccines that have the potential to make an impact on public health and on chronic diseases caused by respiratory viruses[1]." The ongoing Phase 2 trial for Clover's combination vaccine candidates is a randomized, observer-blinded, multi-center study with 420 older adults (60-85 years) enrolled in Australia, and the participants have been randomized to receive either SCB-1022 (RSV + hMPV), SCB-1033 (RSV + hMPV + PIV3) or placebo. Immunogenicity Antibody titers (geometric mean titers [GMTs]) at 28 days post-vaccination in the Phase 2 were generally in-line with or trended higher than the prior Phase 1 trial. Geometric mean fold rises (GMFRs) in neutralizing antibodies (nAbs) at 28 days post-vaccination compared to pre-vaccination: RSV nAbs: Approximately 6-9 fold increases hMPV nAbs: Approximately 6-8 fold increases PIV3 nAbs: Greater than 3 fold increase (approximately 5 fold increase in participants with baseline PIV3 nAbs in the bottom tertile), driven by up to approximately 20 fold increases in PIV3 PreF-specific antibodies[2] No drop-off in antibody responses observed in the oldest participants (75+ years) compared to younger participants (60-74 years). No signs of immune interference on RSV and hMPV nAbs from the addition of PIV3 PreF antigen in SCB-1033 (RSV+hMPV+PIV3) compared to SCB-1022 (RSV+hMPV). Story Continues Respiratory Tract Infections (Based on AE Reporting) Approximately 62% lower rate of respiratory tract infection was observed in the vaccine groups (SCB-1022 and SCB-1033) versus the placebo group within 28 days of vaccination based on AE reporting of any respiratory tract infections (no PCR sequencing of infection cases was conducted in the study). Significant RSV outbreak[3] with co-circulation[4] of hMPV and PIV in Australia occurred during the study enrollment and follow-up period. Safety and Reactogenicity SCB-1022 and SCB-1033 were generally well-tolerated; solicited local and systemic adverse events (AEs) within 7 days of vaccination were mostly mild and all transient. The most common solicited AEs were fatigue, headache and injection site pain, with mean durations of approximately 2 days for the vaccine groups (SCB-1022 and SCB-1033) and the placebo group. The frequency of unsolicited AEs within 28 days of vaccination was similar across the vaccine and placebo groups. There were no vaccine-related serious adverse events (SAEs), AEs of special interest (AESIs), or AEs leading to discontinuation. Commercial-Scale Manufacturing Scale-Up In parallel with the Phase 2 trial, Clover conducted commercial-scale 2,000L bioreactor scale-up production of multiple batches of Trimer-Tagged RSV, hMPV and PIV3 PreF antigen components of SCB-1022/1033. The successful 2,000L production process scale-up further de-risk future late-stage development and commercialization. Based on these positive Phase 2 results for the RSV + hMPV ± PIV3 combination vaccine candidates further validating the Trimer-Tag platform, Clover will continue to evaluate continued mid- and late-stage development plans as well as potential global collaboration opportunities for value maximization.
